failures.contract: (b) Lines. "Only the first 512000 bytes (500 KiB, section 2.5; lane reading: exactly this limit) of the file are read; a leading UTF-8 byte order mark (EF BB BF) is dropped; the rest is decoded as UTF-8 with invalid bytes becoming U+FFFD. Lines end at CR, LF or CRLF. On each line everything from the first # is a comment and removed. A line without : is ignored. The key is the text before the first : with spaces and tabs trimmed, compared ASCII case-insensitively; the value is the text after it with spaces and tabs trimmed. Keys user-agent, allow and disallow are records; every other key (for example sitemap, crawl-delay) is ignored and does not end a group (section 2.2.4). An allow or disallow line before the first user-agent line is ignored (section 2.2.2)."
reasons: exit mismatch: expected one of [0], observed 1 (stderr: )

failures.contract: (c) Groups. "A user-agent line starts a new group unless the previous record was also a user-agent line (blank, comment and ignored lines between them do not count), in which case it adds a name to the current group. The check's userAgent matches a group when it equals one of the group's names compared ASCII case-insensitively. The rules of every matching group are combined. If no group matches, the rules of every group named * are combined. If there is none, no rules apply and every URL is allowed."
reasons: exit mismatch: expected one of [0], observed 1 (stderr: )

failures.contract: (d) Rules. "A rule with an empty value never matches. * in a rule matches any sequence of characters (also none); a $ that is the last character of the rule anchors the match at the end of the path (any other $ is literal). A rule matches when it matches a prefix of the path starting at its first character (or the whole path when anchored). Of the matching rules the one with the longest normalized value (rule (e), counted in octets, * and $ included) decides; when an allow and a disallow of that length both match, allow decides. No matching rule: allowed."
reasons: exit mismatch: expected one of [1], observed 0 (stderr: )

failures.contract: (e) Path and normalization. "The path to match is the URL's path (/ when empty) followed by ? and the query when the query is non-empty; the fragment is never part of it. The path /robots.txt is always allowed when (a) says the file decides. Before comparison both the rule value and the path are normalized: every non-ASCII character becomes its UTF-8 octets percent-encoded with uppercase hex; every %XX escape (two hex digits) of an unreserved character (ASCII letters, digits, -, ., _, ~; RFC 3986) is decoded; every other %XX escape is kept with its hex digits uppercased. Lane reading of the section 2.2.2 examples: reserved characters are never decoded or encoded, so %2F and / differ."
reasons: exit mismatch: expected one of [1], observed 0 (stderr: )
